issues.problem: ctx2 (get travel insurance before the trip) and ctx3 (back up your data now) fit 備えあれば憂いなし (kw017) just as well.
issues.action: Rewrote ctx2 as 'see grandma while you still can' and ctx3 as a dialogue regretting a confession never made: both now centre on regret coming too late.

issues.problem: bad2 'why' was confusing ('saki ni does not mean don't do it in advance').
issues.action: Rewrote: it says regret cannot come before the act, so think ahead; it is not advice to stop worrying about an outcome.

issues.problem: ctx3 (sign up now while you're keen) fits 善は急げ (kw015) as well; ctx1 (I still remember what I learned as a child) was a weak, after-the-fact use.
issues.action: ctx1 rewritten as setting the next goal while the team has momentum from a win; ctx3 rewritten as teaching a son while he is interested.

issues.problem: Story check: the claim that it renders the European proverb 'Strike while the iron is hot' is the standard dictionary account.

issues.idiom: 案ずるより産むが易し
issues.problem: bad2 (no need to plan, put all savings into shares) is a stretch, not clearly wrong to a native speaker: the saying is sometimes used to mean 'just do it'.
issues.action: Replaced it with a clear misuse: calling an easy cake recipe 案ずるより産むが易し when there was no worry beforehand.

issues.idiom: 案ずるより産むが易し

issues.idiom: 好きこそ物の上手なれ
issues.problem: bad2 'why' did not explain the grammar: なれ is the form required after こそ, not an imperative.
issues.action: Clarified that nare is classical (after koso), not an order.
